To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the effects of a nonequilibrium in the translational and vibrational degrees of freedom of the laser molecules can be taken into account by means of an appropriate correction to the rate constant of the reaction that forms HF molecules.
the translational and vibrational relaxation processes in a laser gas medium are the main factors that determine the efficiency and output power of an HF laser.
the effects of a nonequilibrium of translational and rotation of the HF molecules can lead to a substantial reduction in the efficiency of the laser.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a theoretical analysis of the influence of translational and rotation relaxation processes in a laser medium on the specific energy characte-ristics of a cw chemical laser.
the development of the theory of a diffusion-type chemical HF laser.
a theoretical analysis of the effects of the nonequilibrium of the translational motion and rotation of laser molecules on the specific energy charac teristics of a cw chemical laser.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the effect of the translational relaxation on the specific laser energy is small (about 10% of the energy of a laser operating under the conditions of a translational equilibrium) while the rotational relaxation has a strong influence (about 50%).
the influence of translational and/or rotational nonequilibrium is not important in the energy characteristics of a diffusion HF laser.

the effect of the translational nonequilibrium of HF molecules is not very important for the energetics, whereas the effect of the rotational nonequilibrium can be significant and should not be disregarded.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effect of the nonequilibrium of the translational motion and the rotational motion on the specific energy characteristic of a diffusion-type chemical HF laser is small.

the effects of the relaxation of the rotational degrees of freedom of the HF molecules on the specific energy parameters of a diffusion-type cw chemical HF laser are of a secondary nature, while the effects of the translation relaxation are of a primary nature.
the translational and rotation relaxation of laser molecules can significantly influence the specific energy characteristics and efficiency of a diffusion-type cw HF chemical laser.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of a molecular relaxation on the laser energetics can be neglected if the rotational temperature is not too high.
, for a given rate of the rotational relaxation of the laser molecules, the specific output of a cw HF laser increases with an increase in the rate of the translational relaxation of the molecules.

a nonequilibrium of the translational degrees of freedom leads to a decrease in the efficiency of a diffusion-type laser and an increase in its output power, while a nonequilibrium in the rotational degrees of freedom leads only to an increase in the output power.
